summary: Author-of-own-draft delete floor. A non-privileged actor may now DELETE only an application they created themselves AND only while tier='draft'; owner/admin/authoring_draft unchanged; published or someone-else's-draft stays 403; cross-tenant stays 404 (existence never leaks). created_by is written server-side from the authenticated actor, never from the body, and no mutation path can rewrite created_by or flip tier. Cascade extended to cover a genuine pre-existing gap (report_page/list_view/doc_page FK application with no ON DELETE action). All verification re-run independently by the judge — GREEN. No blocking findings.

mutation_probes.predicate_weakened (remove tier==='draft: own-published-403 test went RED as required — 'expected 204 to be 403' (the non-priv author's PUBLISHED app got deleted). Proves the draft-only floor is genuinely enforced by the test, not vacuously green. Reverted via `git checkout -- src/http/applications.ts`; predicate restored byte-identical; git status clean.

forging_probes.created_by_source: written ONLY server-side. createApplication receives actor from the POST route's extractActor (Keycloak sub->slug via resolveActorSlugFromAuth, or dev x-dev-user header) — NEVER from req.body. INSERT column list is fixed; body cannot inject created_by.
forging_probes.update_path_scan: the sole UPDATE choros.application in the codebase (updateApplication) uses a strict column allowlist {section, section_id, display_name, description, sort_order} — created_by and tier are NOT settable. No PATCH/PUT forge vector.
forging_probes.tier_flip: the ONLY writer of application.tier is promoteTier (artifacts.ts), draft->published only, itself authz-gated; there is NO demote (published->draft) path anywhere, and the tier_published_locked trigger blocks published rows. A non-priv actor cannot flip a foreign published app back to draft to make it deletable. No two-step escalation.
forging_probes.verdict: No forge path to gain delete rights over a non-owned or published application.

toctou_probe.finding: The existence read, the tier/created_by read, and the DELETE are all in ONE withTenantTx. The read is `SELECT id, tier, created_by ... FOR UPDATE`, holding the row lock for the whole tx. A concurrent promoteTier either commits before the lock (read sees 'published' -> 403) or blocks until this tx commits (row gone -> promote 404). No window between the ownership decision and the delete.

existence_leak_probe.finding: rowCount===0 returns {kind:'not_found'} (-> 404) BEFORE the ownership/forbidden branch is reached. RLS scopes the SELECT to the caller's tenant, so a foreign-tenant row is invisible and yields 404, never a 403 that would confirm existence. The cross-tenant-same-slug test (created_by='del-actor-c' in TENANT_B, probed by the TENANT_A del-actor-c) pins 404 and that the TENANT_B row survives.
existence_leak_probe.verdict: No existence leak; 404-before-403 ordering correct and pinned.

cascade_completeness.fk_children_of_application: Enumerated live via pg_constraint on template DB: exactly 4 tables FK choros.application(tenant_id,id) — registry_def(application_id), report_page(app_id), doc_page(app_id), list_view(application_id). ALL FOUR now handled: registry_def by step 3 (pre-existing), report_page/doc_page/list_view by the new explicit DELETEs (step 4).
cascade_completeness.no_action_note: these 4 FKs are confdeltype='a' (NO ACTION). Precisely: pre-T-0690 an app-delete with any such child would have been REJECTED (23503 / 409), not silently orphaned — the pr-handoff/comment framing of 'latent orphan risk' is slightly imprecise (blocker, not orphan). Immaterial to correctness: the fix deletes children first so the parent delete succeeds.
cascade_completeness.dependents_cascade: Verified live: report_page_dep->report_page, doc_log->doc_page, doc_ref->doc_page are all ON DELETE CASCADE ('c'); list_view has no dependents; list_view rows scoped by registry_def_id are removed by list_view->registry_def ON DELETE CASCADE in step 3. No orphans, no secondary 409.
cascade_completeness.no_shared_resource_over_delete: report_page/doc_page/list_view each reference a single application (single app_id/application_id) — no cross-application sharing, so nothing belonging to another app is removed. DELETE order (children in step 4 before the application row in step 6) is FK-safe.
cascade_completeness.empirical: the own-draft test seeds report_page + list_view + doc_page (withBindings) and asserts all three rows gone after 204 + audit payload counters report_pages_removed/list_views_removed/doc_pages_removed = 1 each.

migration_probe.shape: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS created_by text NULL — additive, idempotent, nullable, no DEFAULT, no FK, no RLS/PK change. known_tenant_tables.txt not in the diff (unchanged).
migration_probe.null_semantics: the ownership comparison is JS strict equality (appRow.created_by === actor); a legacy NULL comes back as JS null and null===<slug> is false, so pre-migration rows stay owner/admin/authoring_draft-only. No SQL NULL-comparison pitfall (the compare is in TS, not SQL). No composite-FK SET NULL class risk (migration 116) — this is a plain scalar column, no FK.

dead_code: assertMayDeleteConfig fully removed (grep src/ ci/ = 0 refs); the DELETE route resolves resolveActorPrivilege inline (same path) and passes actorIsConfigPrivileged into the cascade. 403 message byte-identical ('not permitted to delete this application').

acceptance_coverage.ac: non-privileged author deletes own draft app -> 204 + full cascade (no orphans)
own published app -> 403 (self-service floor is draft-only)
someone else's draft in same tenant -> 403
authorship-slug match across tenants -> 404 (RLS wins, no existence leak)
owner/admin/authoring_draft behaviour unchanged (deletes foreign/legacy created_by=NULL apps)
created_by written from authenticated actor, not body; no update path rewrites created_by/tier
cascade covers all FK children of application; dependents cascade; FK-safe order

findings.issue: report_page/list_view/doc_page FK application with confdeltype='a' (NO ACTION), so pre-T-0690 an app-delete with any such child would be REJECTED with a 409/23503, not silently orphaned. The comment/handoff call it a 'latent orphan risk'; it is a latent delete-blocker. Immaterial to correctness — the fix (delete children first) is right either way.
findings.suggestion: Optional wording fix: 'latent orphan risk' -> 'latent FK-conflict/409 blocker (children of NO-ACTION FKs)'. No code change.
